title: Reserve pool convertibility pilot: tiered credits, SLA fallbacks, and enterprise questionnaire alignment
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Pilot a Reserve Pool Convertibility model that lets enterprise customers hold reserved GPU credit buckets that can be partially converted to on-demand burst credits, with explicit SLA fallback behavior and contract language for Qs on preemption, data plane isolation, and auditability. The goal is to reduce procurement friction for teams who want a predictable baseline while leaving them flexibility to handle spikes without manual contract amendments.

Problem statement: Current reserved capacity offerings are binary (reserved vs on-demand). Customers ask for: smaller commitment granularity, temporary burst beyond reserved capacity without punitive overage pricing, and deterministic fallback behavior when dedicated nodes are tapped out. Sales/legal also report long review cycles for enterprise security questionnaires when new flexible mechanisms change failure modes or audit trails.

Proposal: Run a 6-week pilot with 3 enterprise customers and an internal simulation workload to validate economics, operational modes, and contract language. Key elements: 1) Reserve buckets measured in GPU-hour credits with three convertibility tiers (soft-burst, firm-burst, emergency-burst) that trade price and preemption guarantees; 2) SLA fallback matrix that specifies latency/throughput targets and automatic model variant routing when reserved capacity is saturated; 3) Billing and telemetry changes to surface converted vs reserved consumption, and tokenized credit reconciliations; 4) Draft enterprise questionnaire responses and contract clauses covering audit logs, KMS usage, preemption windows and indemnity limits.

Pilot mechanics: - Offerable SKUs: Small (8 GPU-hrs/day baseline), Medium (32 GPU-hrs/day), Large (160 GPU-hrs/day). Each SKU can attach a Convertibility Profile: Soft (lower price delta, preemptible at 30min notice), Firm (higher price delta, preemptible at 6hr notice), Emergency (highest price delta, non-preemptible for up to defined burst cap). - Autoscale interplay: Customers keep autoscale enabled for baseline pools; convertibility credits apply only when autoscale cannot fulfill instantaneous demand. - Billing: Split-metering to show reserved consumption, converted-burst consumption, and true on-demand consumption. Provide a reconciliation UI in Console and CSV export. - Observability: Add per-token and per-request tagging to indicate 'reserved', 'converted', or 'ondemand' for cost attribution and SLO dashboards.

Success metrics: - Commercial: 3 pilot customers adopt without extended legal redlines; average spike coverage using convertibility >= 60% of customers' spikes (reducing true on-demand exposure). - Economics: Unit cost to Redwood for converted bursts <= 1.6x baseline reserved unit cost (simulated across pilot workloads). - Operational: No more than one severity-2 incident attributable to convertibility mechanics during the pilot. - Processes: Security questionnaire answers and contractual language approved by Legal and Security within 2 review rounds.

Key deliverables: - Pricing matrix and SKUs, plus example invoice line items for each pilot customer. - Contract appendix language and a worked enterprise questionnaire (SOC/infra questions + preemption description). - Console mockup for Convertibility dashboard and CSV export template. - Billing tagging implementation spec for backend and SDK change notes. - Post-pilot report with adoption, economics, incident reports, and recommendations for general availability.

Open questions / trade-offs: - Granularity: sell in GPU-hrs vs vGPU-minute tokens? Recommendation: GPU-hrs for pilot to reduce billing churn; revisit smaller units in Phase 2. - Preemption notice windows: engineering recommends 6hr minimum to drain KV caches safely; sales/customers ask for 30min. Pilot will include both as separate tiers to collect data. - Legal exposure: emergency non-preemptible bursts raise capacity guarantees that must be capped in contract; Legal proposes a hard cap of 48 hours per calendar month to limit risk. - Metrics fidelity: tagging every request increases tracing volume; ops proposed sampling for low-cost paths and full tagging for enterprise pilot customers only.

Stakeholders: Sales (lead: Priya Nair), Legal (lead: Ben Goldstein), Security (lead: Hana Kim), Engineering (runtime: Tian Li; billing: Omar Hassan), Design (lead: Noa Ruiz)

Acceptance criteria: - Pricing SKUs published internally and testable in staging. - Console mockups reviewed and approved by Design and Eng. - Legal sign-off on contract appendix and questionnaire responses. - Billing and telemetry tags implemented for pilot customers in staging. - 3 enterprise pilot contracts signed (or internal pilot equivalent) by due_date.

Next steps (this ticket): 1) Align with Engineering on billing tag spec (assignee: Marco Diaz). 2) Draft contract appendix and questionnaire answers with Legal (owner: Aisha Patel). 3) Create Console mockups and CSV schema (owner: Noa Ruiz). 4) Kickoff pilot customers list and internal simulation plan (owner: Priya Nair).
comments: 2026-03-05 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket and aligned scope with Sales and Legal. Proposed three convertibility tiers to capture different risk/price trade-offs.

2026-03-07 - Marco Diaz: Engineering reviewed feasibility for tagging and suggested per-customer feature flag to reduce surface area. Raised concern: 30min preemption is risky for long-context workloads due to KV cache inconsistency. Recommended we only offer 30min for small-context batch jobs.
2026-03-08 - Ben Goldstein: Legal drafted initial appendix. Requires explicit cap on continuous emergency-burst hours and indemnity language for capacity shortfalls caused by force majeure.
2026-03-09 - Hana Kim: Security requested KMS/HSM mapping for billing logs and retention constraints; flagged that audit log locations must be included in questionnaire answers.

2026-03-11 - Noa Ruiz: Shared first-pass Console wireframes showing per-SKU credit balances and a reconciliation CSV mock. Design requests product-driven labels for 'converted' vs 'reserved' consumption.
2026-03-12 - Marco Diaz: Billing proto merged to staging branch. Tagging implemented behind flag 'convertibility-pilot'. Need 2 pilot customers to enable testing in staging.
acceptance_criteria: Console mockups approved and dev tickets created
Legal and Security sign-off on appendix and questionnaire
Billing tags present in staging and sample CSVs generated
Pilot customers contracted or internal pilot confirmed
notes_for_sales: Allow sales to offer a two-week free convertibility trial for contracted customers. Provide a one-page appendix summary and FAQ to speed legal review.
risks: Operational risk from preemption windows and KV cache inconsistency, increased tracing cost from tagging, and legal exposure if emergency-burst capacity is under-provisioned.
final_deliverable_format: Post-pilot PDF report, JSON CSV sample exports, and an updated contract appendix text snippet
